intent: Photoreal beauty pass over a dimensionally-correct clay control render (HYBRID render direction of record, docs/DECISIONS-render-assets.md).
engine_contract: Single-track image-edit instruction + one control image. Model choice/fallback lives in the dispatch script (pipeline/scripts/hybrid_render.py), never here.
template: Transform this 3D clay render of a {room_type} into a photorealistic interior photograph. CRITICAL: keep the exact room geometry, camera angle, wall/window/door positions, and the position, size and proportions of every furniture piece and built-in unchanged — the layout is dimensionally accurate and must not move or be redrawn. Replace the flat clay materials with: {material_story}. RELIGHT THE SCENE COMPLETELY — do not keep the flat, even CG illumination of the input: {lighting_story}; build a clear key-light direction with golden warm highlights, deep soft shadow areas and gentle falloff across every wall, glowing warm accents (cove light, bedside or floor lamps) — any cove or LED strip shows gentle intensity variation and soft hot-spots along its run, never a perfectly uniform band — and believable contact shadows under every object. Keep every light source in ONE coherent warm color-temperature family (2700-3000 K residential) — never a cool clinical source against a warm one in the same zone. The mood should read like a magazine interior shot photographed at dusk. Composition: if the immediate foreground is empty, you MAY let one physical element break the camera plane at a frame edge — but only an object that believably STANDS in the room (a potted plant on the floor, the back of a chair, the corner of a side table), softly out of focus and visually grounded, never a cropped pasted prop; if nothing can read naturally there, leave the foreground clean. Never hide the furniture behind it. Styling: dress the room with a SPECIFIC lived-in personality, not showroom-generic — small evidence of a real person's day (an open book left face-down, a half-finished drink on a tray, one slightly rumpled throw), layered textures (wood, ceramic, linen, aged brass), asymmetric arrangements over symmetric ones; you MAY add small decor that does not move or hide the furniture — an area rug under the main furniture group, throw pillows and a draped throw, a few books and a ceramic tray on table surfaces, one potted plant, subtle wall art where a wall is blank. Give the room exactly ONE distinctive design moment aligned with the style direction — a sculptural lamp, one bold piece of wall art, or a single characterful vintage piece — placed where it moves or hides nothing, with everything else kept quiet so the moment reads intentional instead of showroom-safe. Style direction: {style_brief}. Render as a professional interior photograph, NOT a perfect CG image: include subtle real-world imperfection — natural wrinkles and slouch in fabric, slight unevenness in plaster, a hint of lens vignetting and very fine photographic grain — and KILL the classic render tells: any TV or monitor screen must never be a pure-black mirror void (show a soft diffuse reflection of the lit room across it, with a faint dust sheen breaking the gloss); any window or doorway view must have believable depth — a dusk sky gradient, soft-focus foliage or distant city lights with atmospheric haze — never a flat featureless backdrop; wood must show plank-to-plank and panel-to-panel tonal variation, shifts in grain direction and faint wear at edges and touch points, so no two boards read identical; books and paper have slightly splayed, uneven pages. No people, no text, no watermarks, no borders.

slots.room_type: REQUIRED — e.g. 'living room', 'master bedroom suite'; name what each clay mass IS
slots.material_story: comma prose of the target materials

defaults.material_story: warm walnut wood flooring and millwork, boucle and linen upholstery, matte off-white plaster walls, brushed-metal accents
defaults.lighting_story: low warm evening light with one dominant soft key direction, layered with warm cove light and a lit table or floor lamp
defaults.style_brief: contemporary Thai residential, calm and livable, quiet luxury

Layout lock, relight license, CCT family and lived-in styling carried from v004 unchanged.
